scope: Theorem 7.1 (All-level block approximation) of the manuscript “Spectral convergence for critical FK–Ising planar maps” (preprints/Spectral-convergence-for-critical-FK-Ising-planar-maps-October-5-2026/spectral-convergence-critical-fk-ising-planar-maps.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eeb5895c7058765f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 54. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: From an arbitrary sequence of finite spheres, take a further joint representation extraction as in Proposition 2.4 and Proposition 3.1, retaining the interval readouts defined below. Put m = 2n and p = 7/10. Simultaneously for the countable protected interval atlas, the following holds almost surely on activation of an entry (Im, G+ m). There are finite sample-dependent constants j∗, C, and n∗ such that, at every index n ≥ n∗ in the extraction, for every function on V (G+ m) and every integer j ≥ j∗, 1 m X i∈Im |f(v(i)) − (PIm j f)(i)|2 ≤ C 2−pj E0 n(f; G+ m). (7.1) This includes all levels down to and beyond singleton cuts and holds for all functions on the same event. In the two-rooting extraction of Proposition 2.4, one can choose finitely many activated entries from the two rooted atlases such that every corner occurrence belongs to at least one of their intervals, in its corresponding rooted order, for all sufficiently large n.
